chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said:

I asked him about the sign of the Night of Pre-determination, so he said: Its sign is that its wind becomes fragrant; and if it is in cold weather, it becomes warm, and if it is in hot weather, it becomes cool, and thus it becomes pleasant.

He said: And I asked him about the Night of Pre-determination, so he said: The angels and the scribes descend therein to the lowest heaven, so they write what will be of the matters of the year and what will befall the servants. And His Command is Reserved for Him, and in it is the Desire. So He brings forward from it whatever He wills and delays from it whatever He wills, and He obliterates and establishes, and with Him is the Mother of the Book.
ai.seo_question: What are the physical and spiritual signs of the Night of Pre-determination (Laylat al-Qadr) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the dual nature of Laylat al-Qadr, combining sensory signs—such as fragrant air and moderated temperature—with its metaphysical role as the night of divine decree. It highlights the Shia understanding of *al-mahw wa al-isbat* (obliteration and confirmation), where angels record the year's events in the lowest heaven, subject to God's will and ultimately anchored in *Umm al-Kitab*. This reflects the interplay between fixed destiny and divine flexibility, a core concept in Shia eschatology and jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 5<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a sign of the Night of the Pre-determination. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It’s sign is that is wind is aromatic; and if it was during the cold (winter) it warms, and if it was during the hot (summer), it cools, and is pleasant’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked himasws about the Night of Pre-determination, so heasws said: ‘The Angels and the Scribes descend therein to the sky of the world, so they are writing what is to transpire regarding the matters of the year, and what would be hitting the servants. And, its Command is Reserved for Himazwj, and in it is the Desire. So, Heazwj Brings forwards from it whatever Heazwj so Desires to, and Heazwj Delays from it whatever Heazwj so Desires to, and Heazwj [13:39] Obliterates whatever He so Desires to and Establishes, and with Him is the Mother of the Book’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “Once I asked one of the two Imam, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, about signs of the night of destiny. He replied, ‘One of the signs of this night is sweet fragrance; during the cold season it is warm, and during the hot season it is cool and pleasant.’

Someone asked him about the night of destiny. He (the Imam) replied, ‘The angels and scribes come down to the sky above the world and then they write down all that has to happen during the year and what people will experience therein. Its affairs are withheld with Him. In it He has a wish and thus He brings forward whatever He wishes or delays whatever He wishes. He confirms whatever He wishes and deletes whatever He wishes; the mother book is with Him.’”
